column1: # ZAP baseline rules for the CI scan (.github/workflows/ci.yml, E2E job).
# One rule per line, tab separated: <rule id>
# The accepted alerts: IGNORE (does not apply to this site, with the reason) and WARN (a known gap,
# reported but accepted for now). Any other alert fails the build (.zap/check.mjs), so a new
# finding is decided here before it can pass. Rule ids: https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/

column3: CSP: only frame-ancestors so far; a full policy is an open issue (PROJECT_STATUS open issue 17)
Cookie No HttpOnly: only XSRF-TOKEN, which the client must read (double-submit CSRF token); HttpOnly of coinportal.auth and coinportal.af is checked in AuthTests
Dangerous JS Functions: bypassSecurityTrustHtml is Angular's own sanitizer API in the bundle; the app never calls it
Information in Browser localStorage: the UI language preference (coinportal.language), described in the privacy policy
Suspicious Comments: words like "from" in index.html comments
Modern Web Application: informational, the site is an SPA
Re-examine Cache-control Directives: no-cache on pages and no-store on API data are deliberate (Hosting/SpaHosting, SecurityHeaders)
Storable and Cacheable Content: hashed client files are immutable, the rest revalidates; deliberate

Source Code Disclosure - File Inclusion (active scan): v= of an image URL is a GUID and files are found by ids only; both answers are the same 400, they differ only in the traceId (74-75% against a 75% threshold)
Cookie Slack Detector (active scan, informational): signed-out scan, the responses do not depend on the antiforgery cookies by design

User Controllable HTML Element Attribute (informational): the server sends the same static index.html for every page, nothing from the address goes into the HTML; it matched dir=Desc against the word "description" of a meta tag
